isolation.runtime: docker 29.5.2 (daemon Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS); Docker Desktop VM with 2 CPUs / 4 GB
isolation.network_policy: off-loopback HTTP aborted; WebSocket closed; web fonts/favicons stubbed locally; each entry is supervised by an external `timeout -s KILL` so a page that blocks the driver is recorded as TIMEOUT_ABORTED instead of stalling the run
isolation.input_attribution: a difference after synthetic input is attributed to input only when the same channel was stable during the idle baseline; see scripts/input_attribution.py
isolation.retry_configuration: 8 entries that could not be measured at --memory 1g / 60 s were re-run once at --memory 2g / 120 s. One (aurora-over-the-fjord) then loaded cleanly, i.e. it needed more time rather than being broken; the other 7 reproduced (2 renderer crashes, 2 iframe bounding-box timeouts, 1 iframe never visible, 3 hard blocks whose child produced no output at all).

evidence_scope: Produced inside a disposable container with --network none, a read-only rootfs, a read-only artifact mount, dropped capabilities and a non-root user. INPUT_RESPONSIVE means rendered output changed after synthetic pointer/keyboard input AND the same channel was stable during the idle baseline; a difference on a page that repaints on its own is recorded as INPUT_RESPONSE_NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE instead (see scripts/input_attribution.py). It does not prove correctness, completeness or authorship. A blocked request means the artifact needs the network, which is a dependency finding, not necessarily a defect. counts.gameplay_verified is always 0 in this artifact: the strongest claim a machine may make here is counts.input_responsive.
